Exposure is child age in days on Election Day, represented by timing-category indicators; outcome is register-recorded local-election turnout. No pre-treatment control in the inventory covers labor-force status, and the listed controls are not reasonable proxies for it: education, marital status, and family composition do not reliably capture whether someone is employed, unemployed, entering or leaving the labor force, or their occupational status. The municipality and district fixed effects absorb geographic variation, not individual labor-force status; the narrow childbirth-timing sample restriction does not adjust for it. Thus no control or design feature handles this confounder.
